notes: ACCESS: Tier (a) direct HTTP (curl_cffi impersonate=chrome) worked for all pages; robots.txt (https://www.oliverbonas.com/robots.txt) has no blanket Disallow and does not name anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web, so plain HTTP fetch is permitted. Escalated to Playwright headless (tier b) only for a handful of pages whose grid uses lazy-load without a numeric 'See all' button (Cushions, Bedding, Jewellery Storage, and a spot-check of Bedroom Accessories/Storage) to scroll-stabilize the true rendered product count; no anti-bot wall was hit so tier (c) was never needed. TREE: union of the site's mega-menu (embedded in the SSR HTML of /homeware), the XML sitemap (https://www.oliverbonas.com/sitemap.xml, 6565 urls), and each category page's own breadcrumb JSON-LD. Two distinct hierarchies found: 'Home Furnishings' (/homeware/soft-furnishings) is a real 3-level parent with nested child URLs (cushions/doormats/rugs/throws) confirmed via breadcrumb JSON-LD, so it is recorded as a grouping row; Bedding/Quilts(bedspreads)/Bath Mats/Kitchen Textiles/Storage/Storage Baskets/Seagrass Baskets/Storage Hooks(hooks)/Wine Racks all show a flat 2-level 'Homeware > X' breadcrumb (their shared internal parent id 247 is not exposed as a navigable node), so they are recorded as flat leaves with no artificial group parent. QTY: preferred the front-end 'See all N items' load-more button text found in the raw HTML (site's own displayed total) wherever present (Doormats 15, Rugs 17, Throws 19, Bedspreads/Quilts 6, Bath Mats 6, Kitchen Textiles 21, Storage 73, Storage Baskets 12, Storage Hooks 30). Where no such button exists (Cushions, Bedding, Jewellery Storage), used Playwright to scroll the grid to a stable unique-product-link count. Wine Racks confirmed 0 via literal 'There are no results matching your selection' page text (storage.md zero-product-category rule). Seagrass Baskets confirmed 1 via a single rendered product card with no load-more control. The backend '/api/n/route/...' JSON endpoint was tested but discarded as evidence: its 'products' array is a raw catalog assignment list that does not reflect the storefront (e.g. it listed 93 products for Jewellery Storage vs 1 actually ever rendered/paginated to a shopper, and listed products for Wine Racks despite the page showing zero results), consistent with prior project finding that storefront count APIs are inflated. EXCLUDED: 'Bedroom Accessories' (424 items, /homeware/category/bedroom-accessories) - a mixed cross-listing hub (mirrors, diffusers, candles, lamps per its own quick-links) not a pure textile or storage category, so dropped per the room-name-alone rule. 'Placemats & Coasters' (/homeware/category/coasters-placemats, 7 items) - sampled products are resin/marble coasters, not fabric placemats, so Kitchen & Dining not Textile, out of scope. by-room hub pages (bathroom/kitchen/living-room/hallway/home-office/dining-room/garden) - mixed multi-category landing pages, not single-type categories. /furniture/storage and /furniture/storage/lockers - site explicitly places these in the Furniture department/nav, so per storage.md rule 21/27 they belong to Furniture.xlsx (already validated, not touched here), excluded from Storage.xlsx. No curtains, tablecloths, table runners, napkins, tapestries, or outdoor textiles found anywhere in the nav/sitemap union - the site does not sell them. 'Jewellery Storage' (/jewellery/jewellery-storage, 1 item, Pierre The Cat Ring Holder) included at LOW confidence: it is a genuine storage/organizer product per storage.md rule 7 but sits in the site's Jewellery department, not Homeware, so it is a borderline home-storage-vs-personal-accessory call flagged for review. 'Storage Hooks' (/homeware/category/hooks) included at MEDIUM confidence: products are decorative wall/over-door hooks explicitly named 'Storage Hooks' by the site (h1), functionally hanging-storage/organization rather than pure wall decor. 'Wine Racks' included at MEDIUM confidence per storage.md rule 19 (racks) despite currently zero products.
